newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt to review 1997 budget end January.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt to review 1997 budget end January.

text.p: The Belgian government will bring its annual budget review forward to the end of January from the usual February/March time, following an overshoot of its 1996 budget deficit target, it said on Friday.

"The government has taken a first series of correcting measures in the health sector in December. At the 1997 budget review at the end of January we will see if an additional effort is necessary," Budget Minister Herman Van Rompuy told a news conference.
"If the 10 billion Belgian francs worth of measures taken in December suffice, then we will have an easy budget review. If they do not we will take extra measures," Van Rompuy said.
The Belgian 1996 budget deficit fell to 3.4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from 4.1 percent in 1995, the government said on Friday.

The original target for the 1996 budget deficit, set in October 1995, was 3.0 percent, although this was raised to 3.3 percent in October 1996 on grounds of more sluggish than expected economic growth.
Van Rompuy said the government remained committed to cutting the deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP in 1997 to qualify for participation in the single European currency.
